This is the primary condition for this resource.

Possible reasons for this condition to be True are:

operator_config.name: RewriteReasonAccepted
operator_config.doc:
RewriteReasonAccepted indicates the rewrite is valid, non-conflicting,
and has been successfully applied to the inference pool.

operator_config.name: RewriteReasonPending

RewriteReasonPending is the initial state, and indicates that the
controller has not yet reconciled the InferenceModelRewrite.

operator_config.name: ObjectiveConditionAccepted

ObjectiveConditionAccepted indicates if the objective config is accepted, and if not, why.

Possible reasons for this condition to be True are:

* "Accepted"

Possible reasons for this condition to be Unknown are:

* "Pending"

operator_config.name: AddToScheme
operator_config.doc:
AddToScheme adds all types of this clientset into the given scheme. This allows composition
of clientsets, like in:

	import (
	  "k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes"
	  clientsetscheme "k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes/scheme"
	  aggregatorclientsetscheme "k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/client/clientset_generated/clientset/scheme"
	)

	kclientset, _ := kubernetes.NewForConfig(c)
	_ = aggregatorclientsetscheme.AddToScheme(clientsetscheme.Scheme)

After this, RawExtensions in Kubernetes types will serialize kube-aggregator types
correctly.

operator_config.name: enableExperimentalFlowControlLayer
operator_config.doc:
enableExperimentalFlowControlLayer defines the environment variable used as a feature flag for the pluggable flow
control layer.
DEPRECATION NOTICE - this env var will be removed in the next version as we switch to configuring the EPP using FeatureGates in the config file.

operator_config.name: metricsShutdownTimeout
operator_config.doc:
metricsShutdownTimeout bounds graceful shutdown of the metrics server so a
scraper holding a connection at process exit cannot block termination.

operator_config.name: debounceDelay
operator_config.doc: debounceDelay wait for events to settle before reloading

operator_config.name: BodyByteLimit
operator_config.doc:
BodyByteLimit is the max limit of 62Kb per streamed chunk.
Certain envoy implementations set a max limit of 64Kb per streamed chunk, intentionally setting this lower for a safe margin.

operator_config.name: RequestDroppedReasonEvicted
operator_config.doc:
Evicted — request was dispatched to an inference server and then killed.
The generic "evicted" reason is the current default used by ImmediateResponseEvictor.Evict().
The specific sub-reasons are forward-looking for when EvictN() callers specify why they're evicting.

operator_config.name: RequestDroppedReasonHeaderKey
operator_config.doc:
RequestDroppedReasonHeaderKey is the HTTP response header that communicates the specific
reason a request was dropped by flow control.

operator_config.name: RequestDroppedReasonSaturated
operator_config.doc: Rejected — request never reached an inference server.

operator_config.name: atomicLevel
operator_config.doc:
atomicLevel is shared between InitSetupLogging and InitLogging so the log
level can be adjusted after the controller-runtime delegation is fulfilled.

operator_config.name: DataParallelEndpointHeader
operator_config.doc: DataParallelEndpointHeader is the header name used to indicate the worker <ip:port> for Data Parallel

operator_config.name: EncoderEndpointsHeader
operator_config.doc: EncoderEndpointsHeader is the header name used to indicate Encoder workers <ip:port> list

operator_config.name: InferencePoolAPIGroup
operator_config.doc: InferencePoolAPIGroup is the default InferencePool API group

operator_config.name: KVCacheSourceHeader
operator_config.doc:
KVCacheSourceHeader is the header name used to indicate the worker <ip:port> holding
the most cached prefix KV blocks for the request, to pull from over the P2P connector
instead of recomputing them

operator_config.name: PreferHeader
operator_config.doc:
PreferHeader is the standard HTTP "Prefer" header (RFC 7240). EPP
receives header keys lowercased.

operator_config.name: PreferIfAvailable
operator_config.doc:
PreferIfAvailable is the preference token the coordinator sets to mark a
request as a speculative early-decode attempt: route to a decode worker
only if its KV cache already covers the prompt (at least partially); otherwise EPP surfaces
412 Precondition Failed so the coordinator restarts the pipeline.

operator_config.name: PrefillEndpointHeader
operator_config.doc: PrefillEndpointHeader is the header name used to indicate Prefill worker <ip:port>

operator_config.name: maxValueLen
operator_config.doc:
maxValueLen caps a logged header value. Longer values are truncated so a
verbose metadata header does not dominate the log line.

operator_config.name: BytesPerMB
operator_config.doc: BytesPerMB is the number of bytes in one megabyte.

operator_config.name: DefaultMaxRequestBodySize
operator_config.doc:
DefaultMaxRequestBodySize is the default cap for server.max_request_body_size,
in megabytes. It is generous enough to accommodate multimodal requests that
inline images as data: URIs; text-only deployments can lower it.

operator_config.name: DefaultECConnectorName
operator_config.doc:
DefaultECConnectorName is the EC connector selected when an empty string is
passed to Build. Defaults to ec-shared-storage (no-op on the wire).

operator_config.name: loggerName
operator_config.doc:
loggerName is the WithName scope applied to the context logger in connector
log lines.

operator_config.name: DefaultKVConnectorName
operator_config.doc:
DefaultKVConnectorName is the KV connector selected when an empty string is
passed to Build. Defaults to kv-shared-storage (no-op on the wire).

operator_config.name: loggerName
operator_config.doc:
loggerName is the WithName scope applied to the context logger in connector
log lines.

operator_config.name: maxRedactDepth
operator_config.doc:
maxRedactDepth caps redactStrings recursion so a deeply nested adversarial
body cannot drive it toward the 500-level encoding/json limit on a trace log.

operator_config.name: maxRedactElems
operator_config.doc: maxRedactElems caps how many array elements are kept before a count marker.

operator_config.name: maxRedactRawBodyLen
operator_config.doc: maxRedactRawBodyLen bounds a non-JSON body logged verbatim.

operator_config.name: maxRedactStringLen
operator_config.doc:
maxRedactStringLen is the longest JSON string value kept verbatim; longer
values are replaced with a marker so tensor blobs, base64, and URLs do not
drown out the structural fields.

operator_config.name: ErrBadRequest
operator_config.doc:
ErrBadRequest marks a step failure as caused by invalid client input rather
than an internal or upstream fault. Steps wrap it (with %w) when rejecting a
malformed request so the server can answer 400 instead of 502.

operator_config.name: ErrPipelineDone
operator_config.doc:
ErrPipelineDone is returned by a step to signal successful early exit.
The pipeline treats this as success and stops executing further steps.

operator_config.name: validRequestID
operator_config.doc:
validRequestID bounds a client-supplied x-request-id to alphanumerics and
dashes, at most 128 characters. handleInference replaces a header that fails
the match with a generated UUID before it reaches error responses; the
request-logging middleware redacts it. This keeps attacker-controlled content
out of both surfaces.

operator_config.name: errCacheMiss
operator_config.doc:
errCacheMiss signals that the conditional-decode cache probe returned 412.
It flows from the proxy's ModifyResponse to its ErrorHandler, which swallows
it so the miss can fall through to the rest of the pipeline.

operator_config.name: allowedImageContentTypes
operator_config.doc:
allowedImageContentTypes is the set of data URI media types a vision model
accepts. Non-image payloads (HTML, SVG, scripts, audio, video) are rejected
so they are not inlined and forwarded downstream.

operator_config.name: cgnatBlock
operator_config.doc:
cgnatBlock is the RFC 6598 carrier-grade NAT range, which net.IP has no
dedicated predicate for.

operator_config.name: defaultMaxDownloadSize
operator_config.doc: defaultMaxDownloadSize is the default cap for max_download_size, in megabytes.

operator_config.name: errBlockedAddress
operator_config.value: fmt.Errorf("address resolves to a blocked range: %w", pipeline.ErrBadRequest)
operator_config.doc:
errBlockedAddress marks a dial to a forbidden address. It wraps
pipeline.ErrBadRequest so the connection failure surfaced by http.Client.Do
(wrapped in *url.Error/*net.OpError, both of which Unwrap) classifies as a
client 4xx rather than a 502.

operator_config.name: maxErrorBodySize
operator_config.doc:
maxErrorBodySize caps how much of a non-2xx upstream response body is read
into memory, bounding OOM exposure to an adversarial upstream pod.

operator_config.name: DefaultScorerWeight
operator_config.doc: DefaultScorerWeight is the weight used for scorers referenced in the configuration without explicit weights.

operator_config.name: ErrDuplicateExtractorType
operator_config.value: errors.New("duplicate extractor type configured for the same source")

operator_config.doc: compile-time type assertion

operator_config.name: activePortsAnnotation
operator_config.doc:
activePortsAnnotation is used to specify which ports on a pod should be considered
as active for inference traffic. The value should be a comma-separated list of port numbers.
Example: "8000,8001,8002"

operator_config.name: errPoolNotSynced
operator_config.value: errors.New("InferencePool is not initialized in data store")

operator_config.name: errRegistrationDropped
operator_config.value: errors.New("endpoint registration dropped: collector already registered or failed to start")
operator_config.doc:
errRegistrationDropped reports an endpoint that could not be tracked: its collector is
still registered from an earlier registration (an upsert overlapping an in-flight delete)
or failed to start. Callers match it with errors.Is to decide whether to retry.

operator_config.name: legacyGAIEActivePortsAnnotation
operator_config.doc:
legacyGAIEActivePortsAnnotation is the legacy GAIE active ports annotation key, kept for backward compatibility.

Deprecated: use activePortsAnnotation instead; this may be removed in a future release.

operator_config.name: ErrFlowIDEmpty
operator_config.doc: ErrFlowIDEmpty indicates that a flow specification was provided with an empty flow ID.

operator_config.name: ErrFlowInstanceNotFound
operator_config.doc: ErrFlowInstanceNotFound indicates that a requested flow instance (a `ManagedQueue`) does not exist.

operator_config.name: ErrInvalidQueueItemHandle
operator_config.doc:
ErrInvalidQueueItemHandle indicates that a QueueItemHandle provided to a SafeQueue operation (e.g.,
SafeQueue.Remove()) is not valid for that queue, has been invalidated, or does not correspond to an actual item in
the queue.

operator_config.name: ErrPriorityBandNotFound
operator_config.doc: ErrPriorityBandNotFound indicates that a requested priority band does not exist in the registry configuration.

operator_config.name: ErrQueueItemNotFound
operator_config.value: errors.New("queue item not found for the given handle")
operator_config.doc:
ErrQueueItemNotFound indicates that a SafeQueue.Remove(handle) operation did not find an item matching the
provided, valid QueueItemHandle. This can occur if the item was removed by a concurrent operation.

operator_config.name: defaultEnqueueChannelBufferSize
operator_config.doc: defaultEnqueueChannelBufferSize is the default size of a worker's incoming request buffer.

operator_config.name: defaultExpiryCleanupInterval
operator_config.doc: defaultExpiryCleanupInterval is the default frequency for scanning for expired items.

operator_config.name: ErrProcessorBusy
operator_config.doc:
ErrProcessorBusy is a sentinel error returned by the processor's Submit method indicating that the processor's
internal buffer is momentarily full and cannot accept new work.

operator_config.name: maxCleanupWorkers
operator_config.doc:
maxCleanupWorkers caps the number of concurrent workers for background cleanup tasks. This prevents the processor
from overwhelming the Go scheduler with too many goroutines.

operator_config.name: PriorityQueueName
operator_config.doc:
PriorityQueueName identifies the priority queue implementation (used for benchmark labels).

This queue provides a concurrent-safe priority queue whose ordering is maintained by an internal
container/heap. Items are ordered by the configured OrderingPolicy, with the highest-priority
item (per the policy) at the head.

Each item's position in the heap is tracked on its handle, enabling O(log n) targeted removal.

operator_config.name: DefaultFairnessPolicyRef
operator_config.doc: DefaultFairnessPolicyRef is the default policy for selecting which flow's queue to service next.

operator_config.name: DefaultOrderingPolicyRef
operator_config.doc: DefaultOrderingPolicyRef is the default policy for selecting items within a single flow's queue.

operator_config.name: DefaultUsageLimitPolicyRef
operator_config.doc: DefaultUsageLimitPolicyRef is the default policy to compute usage limit of a priority band dynamically.

operator_config.name: defaultFlowGCTimeout
operator_config.doc:
defaultFlowGCTimeout is the default duration of inactivity after which an idle flow is garbage collected.
This also serves as the interval for the periodic garbage collection scan.

operator_config.name: defaultPriorityBandGCTimeout
operator_config.doc:
defaultPriorityBandGCTimeout is the default duration of inactivity after which a dynamically provisioned
priority band is garbage collected. Set to 2x flow GC timeout to ensure flows are cleaned up first.

operator_config.name: defaultPriorityBandMaxBytes
operator_config.doc:
defaultPriorityBandMaxBytes is the default global capacity for a priority band if not explicitly configured.
It is set to 1 GB.

operator_config.name: ErrContextCancelled
operator_config.doc:
ErrContextCancelled indicates a request was evicted because its associated context (from
`FlowControlRequest.Context()`) was cancelled. This error typically wraps the underlying `context.Canceled` or
`context.DeadlineExceeded` error.

operator_config.name: ErrEvicted
operator_config.doc:
ErrEvicted is a sentinel error indicating a request was removed from a queue *after* being successfully enqueued,
but for reasons other than successful dispatch (e.g., TTL expiry, displacement). Errors returned by
`FlowController.EnqueueAndWait()` that signify post-queue eviction will wrap this error.

Callers should use `errors.Is(err, ErrEvicted)` to check for this general class of failure.

operator_config.name: ErrFlowControllerNotRunning
operator_config.doc:
ErrFlowControllerNotRunning indicates that an operation could not complete or an item was evicted because the
`controller.FlowController` is not running or is in the process of shutting down.

When returned by `FlowController.EnqueueAndWait()`, this will be wrapped by `ErrRejected` (if rejection happens
before internal queuing) or `ErrEvicted` (if eviction happens after internal queuing).

operator_config.name: ErrNoEndpoints
operator_config.doc:
ErrNoEndpoints indicates that a request was rejected at the queue-capacity boundary while the candidate pool had no
endpoints. The queue acts as a scale-from-zero waiting room; when it fills with no backends to drain it, the
rejection reflects genuine unavailability rather than backpressure against a contended pool.

operator_config.name: ErrQueueAtCapacity
operator_config.doc: ErrQueueAtCapacity indicates that a request could not be enqueued because queue capacity limits were met.

operator_config.name: ErrRejected
operator_config.doc:
ErrRejected is a sentinel error indicating a request was rejected by the `controller.FlowController` *before* being
formally enqueued. Errors returned by `FlowController.EnqueueAndWait()` that signify pre-queue rejection will wrap
this error.

Callers should use `errors.Is(err, ErrRejected)` to check for this general class of failure.

operator_config.name: ErrTTLExpired
operator_config.doc: ErrTTLExpired indicates a request was evicted from a queue because its effective Time-To-Live expired.

operator_config.name: ErrIncompatiblePriorityType
operator_config.value: errors.New("incompatible priority score type for comparison")
operator_config.doc:
ErrIncompatiblePriorityType indicates that a FairnessPolicy attempted to compare items from two different flow
queues whose ItemComparators have different ScoreType values, making a meaningful comparison impossible.

operator_config.name: cleanupInterval
operator_config.doc: cleanupInterval defines the periodic interval that the cleanup go routine uses to check for stale data.

operator_config.name: stalenessThreshold
operator_config.doc:
stalenessThreshold defines the threshold for considering data as stale.
if data of a request hasn't been read/write in the last "stalenessThreshold", it is considered as stale data
and will be cleaned in the next cleanup cycle.

operator_config.name: DefaultProducerRegistry
operator_config.doc:
DefaultProducerRegistry maps a data key to the default producer plugin name (same as type).
Populated via RegisterAsDefaultProducer.

operator_config.name: PluginsWithPluginDependencies
operator_config.doc: PluginsWithPluginDependencies maps plugin types to their configuration parser function, used to determine plugin dependencies

operator_config.name: Registry
operator_config.doc: Registry is a mapping from plugin type to Factory function.

operator_config.name: ErrNotFound
operator_config.doc: ErrNotFound is the not found error message.

operator_config.name: Affinity
operator_config.doc:
Affinity indicates a scorer that prefers endpoints with existing locality, such as kv-cache or session-related state,
and therefore tends to give higher scores to the same endpoints.

operator_config.name: Balance
operator_config.doc: Balance indicates a scorer that its preference is balanced between Affinity and Distribution.

operator_config.name: Distribution
operator_config.doc:
Distribution indicates a scorer that prefers spreading requests evenly across all candidate endpoints to avoid
hotspots and improve overall utilization.

operator_config.name: InFlightLoadDataKey
operator_config.doc:
InFlightLoadDataKey carries the per-endpoint in-flight load snapshot used by
load-aware scorers. Populated by InFlightLoadProducer.Produce on each
candidate endpoint at the start of every scheduling cycle.

Represents the live, real-time load on the endpoint (tokens and requests),
injected dynamically and never overwritten during a scheduling cycle.

operator_config.name: UncachedRequestTokensDataKey
operator_config.doc:
UncachedRequestTokensDataKey carries the projected impact of the current request
on a specific endpoint. Populated statically during scheduling.

operator_config.name: DCGMExtractorType
operator_config.doc: DCGMExtractorType is the plugin type for the DCGM metrics extractor.

operator_config.name: GPUUtilizationDataKey
operator_config.doc:
GPUUtilizationDataKey identifies per-endpoint GPU utilization published
by the DCGM extractor and consumed by GPU-aware filters and scorers.

operator_config.name: EncoderCacheMatchInfoKey
operator_config.doc:
EncoderCacheMatchInfoKey is attached to endpoints by the multimodal data
producer and consumed by scorer/latency plugins that need encoder-cache locality.

operator_config.name: SpeculativeTierKey
operator_config.doc:
SpeculativeTierKey is the CachedBlocksByTier key for speculative index
entries, which carry no engine-reported device tier.

operator_config.name: SessionIDDataKey
operator_config.doc:
SessionIDDataKey identifies the session identifier published on the request
attribute store. The default producer is the session-id-producer.

operator_config.name: TopologyAttributeKey
operator_config.doc: TopologyAttributeKey identifies the Topology attribute stored on each endpoint.

operator_config.name: TopologyExtractorType
operator_config.doc: TopologyExtractorType is the plugin type identifier for the topology extractor.

operator_config.name: KVCacheUsagePercentKey
operator_config.doc: --- Internal Keys (for Legacy/Gauge Usage) ---

operator_config.name: LoraInfoRunningAdaptersMetricName
operator_config.doc: LoRA metrics based on MSP

operator_config.name: defaultEngineName
operator_config.doc: defaultEngineName is the default engine used when defaultEngine is not specified.

operator_config.name: DefaultEngineType
operator_config.doc: DefaultEngineType is the key for the fallback mapping.

operator_config.name: DefaultEngineTypeLabelKey
operator_config.doc: DefaultEngineTypeLabelKey is the default label on Pods that indicates the inference engine type.

operator_config.name: legacyGAIEEngineTypeLabelKey
operator_config.doc:
legacyGAIEEngineTypeLabelKey is the legacy GAIE label key, kept for backward compatibility.

Deprecated: use DefaultEngineTypeLabelKey instead; this may be removed in a future release.

operator_config.name: addQuotesRE
operator_config.doc: addQuotesRE is the compiled form of the pattern used by addQuotesToLabelValues.

operator_config.name: labelPairRE
operator_config.doc:
labelPairRE handles structural parsing: extracts the key and value from a key="value" label pair
(after addQuotesToLabelValues normalisation). Field validation (label name syntax) is delegated
to model.LegacyValidation.IsValidLabelName.

operator_config.name: metricSpecRE
operator_config.doc:
metricSpecRE handles structural parsing: extracts the metric name token and optional label block.
Field validation (metric name syntax) is delegated to model.LegacyValidation.IsValidMetricName.

ModelExtractor is not a requesthandling.DataProducer as data here is produced
asynchronously and not tied to incoming requests

operator_config.name: podGVK
operator_config.doc: podGVK is the core/v1 Pod GVK watched by the pod notification handler.

operator_config.name: baseTransport
maxIdleConnections
operator_config.doc:
the maximum idle connection count is shared by all endpoints. The value is
set high to ensure the number of idle connection is above the expected
endpoint count. Setting it too low would cause thrashing of the idle connection
pool and incur higher overheads for every GET (e.g., socket initiation, certificate
exchange, connections in timed wait state, etc.).

operator_config.name: maxIdleConnsPerHost
operator_config.doc:
allow some grace when connections are not made idle immediately (e.g., parsing
and updating might take some time). This allows maintaining up to two idle connections
per endpoint (defined as scheme://host:port).

operator_config.name: defaultStepTimeout
operator_config.doc:
defaultStepTimeout bounds each Poll and each Extract independently so a slow
extractor cannot starve sibling extractors of their tick budget.

operator_config.name: EndpointNotificationSourceType
operator_config.doc: EndpointNotificationSourceType is the plugin type identifier for endpoint notification sources.

operator_config.name: NotificationSourceType
operator_config.doc: NotificationSourceType is the plugin type identifier for k8s notification sources.

operator_config.name: SheddableFilterType
operator_config.doc:
SheddableFilterType only admits sheddable requests (priority < 0) into the eviction queue.
This uses the project-wide definition of sheddable from requtil.IsSheddable.

operator_config.name: PriorityThenTimeOrderingType
operator_config.doc:
PriorityThenTimeOrderingType evicts the lowest priority request first,
breaking ties by newest dispatch time (least KV-cache investment).

operator_config.name: GlobalStrictFairnessPolicyType
operator_config.doc: GlobalStrictFairnessPolicyType is the registration type for the global strict fairness policy.

operator_config.name: enqueueTimeAttributeKey
operator_config.doc:
enqueueTimeAttributeKey is the per-request attribute under which Pick
stashes the flow-control enqueue timestamp for PreRequest to read back.

operator_config.name: RoundRobinFairnessPolicyType
operator_config.doc: RoundRobinFairnessPolicyType is the registration type for the round-robin fairness policy.

operator_config.name: EDFOrderingPolicyType
operator_config.doc:
EDFOrderingPolicyType is the registration type for the EDF ordering policy.

It selects the request with the earliest absolute deadline.
For detailed documentation, see README.md.

operator_config.name: FCFSOrderingPolicyType
operator_config.doc:
FCFSOrderingPolicyType is the registration type for the FCFS ordering policy.

It selects the item with the earliest logical enqueue time.
For detailed documentation on behavior and queue pairing, see README.md.

operator_config.name: SLODeadlineOrderingPolicyType
operator_config.doc:
SLODeadlineOrderingPolicyType is the registration type for the SLO deadline ordering policy.

It selects the request with the earliest SLO-based deadline.
For detailed documentation, see README.md.

operator_config.name: sloTtftHeader
operator_config.doc: sloTtftHeader is the request header name for SLO time-to-first-token in milliseconds.

operator_config.name: defaultConcurrencyMode
operator_config.doc: defaultConcurrencyMode is used when ConcurrencyMode is unset.

operator_config.name: defaultHeadroom
operator_config.doc: defaultHeadroom is the default burst allowance (0%).

operator_config.name: defaultMaxConcurrency
operator_config.doc: defaultMaxConcurrency is the safe baseline for many LLM serving engines.

operator_config.name: defaultMaxTokenConcurrency
operator_config.doc: defaultMaxTokenConcurrency is the default maximum number of tokens allowed per endpoint.

operator_config.name: modeRequests
operator_config.doc: modeRequests uses request count for concurrency detection.

operator_config.name: modeTokens
operator_config.doc: modeTokens uses token count for concurrency detection.

operator_config.name: DefaultKVCacheUtilThreshold
operator_config.doc: DefaultKVCacheUtilThreshold is the default KV cache utilization (0.0 to 1.0) threshold.

operator_config.name: DefaultMetricsStalenessThreshold
operator_config.doc:
DefaultMetricsStalenessThreshold defines how old metrics can be before they are considered
stale.

operator_config.name: DefaultQueueDepthThreshold
operator_config.doc: DefaultQueueDepthThreshold is the default waiting queue size threshold.

operator_config.name: defaultHeadroom
operator_config.doc: defaultHeadroom is the default burst allowance (0%).

operator_config.name: UtilizationDetectorType
operator_config.doc: UtilizationDetectorType is the unique identifier for this plugin.

operator_config.name: domainRank
operator_config.doc: domainRank maps by ordinal rank, ignoring numerical priority values.

operator_config.name: domainValue
operator_config.doc: domainValue maps proportionally to numerical priority values.

operator_config.name: shapeLinear
operator_config.doc:
shape constants define the interpolation curve applied across the ceiling range.
Only "linear" is supported; additional shapes (sigmoid, exponential, step, etc.) may be added.

operator_config.name: PolicyType
operator_config.doc: PolicyType is the registration type for the priority holdback usage limit policy.

operator_config.name: PolicyType
operator_config.doc:
PolicyType is the registration string. The YAML "type:" field in
pluginsCustomConfig must equal this value for the loader to find the
factory.
compile-time validation

operator_config.name: Type
operator_config.doc: Type is the registered plugin type for the probabilistic admitter.
compile-time interface assertion

operator_config.name: TracerScope
operator_config.doc:
TracerScope is the OTel instrumentation scope shared by all plugins under
the requestcontrol framework component.

operator_config.name: ApproxPrefixCachePluginType
operator_config.doc: ApproxPrefixCachePluginType is the default producer type for PrefixCacheMatchInfoDataKey.

operator_config.name: minBlockSizeTokens
operator_config.doc:
minBlockSizeTokens is the floor applied to the block size returned by
GetBlockSize. The routing-side indexer keeps one LRU entry per (pod, block),
so very small block sizes cause gigabyte-scale memory growth at scale. 64
tokens is coarse enough to bound memory while still preserving useful
prefix-match signal. Defined as a var so tests in this package can lower it
to exercise prefix-match logic at small block sizes without leaking a knob
into the public configuration surface. See
https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d-router/issues/1158.

operator_config.name: defaultBlockSizeTokens
operator_config.doc: defaultBlockSizeTokens is the default token block size (vLLM default is 16).

operator_config.name: defaultLRUCapacityPerServer
operator_config.doc:
defaultLRUCapacityPerServer is the default capacity of the LRU indexer per server.
The indexer is an approximation to the actual prefix LRU cache state on the model servers per server (pod).
A small capacity ensures a high accuracy of cache hit on the model server, but it will
increase the chance of false negatives. A high capacity does the opposite.
To properly size this, consider the sum of the total number of cache entries on all model
servers. Consider the llama3 8B model on a H100 80GB GPUs. The size of the model weight is
about 16GB. The remaining HBM used for caching prefixes is 64GB. Each
token is about 128KB in size, so we can cache 500K tokens. Using the default block size of 16
in vLLM, we will have 250K / 16 = 31.25K blocks.

operator_config.name: defaultMaxPrefixBlocks
operator_config.doc:

MaxPrefixTokensToMatch is 0 and MaxPrefixBlocksToMatch is non-zero; the
default token cap otherwise supersedes it.
Two long requests with the same prefix up to this limit will be indistinguishable.
This parameter provides a trade-off between cache size, prefix matching speed and matching
accuracy. Use a small value if most requests are short to reduce cache size and speed up the
matching process. Use a large value if most requests are long to increase the matching accuracy.

operator_config.name: defaultMaxPrefixTokens
operator_config.doc:
defaultMaxPrefixTokens caps prefix matching at the context window of large
production models (128K tokens, e.g. gpt-oss 120b), a reasonable upper bound
that covers the long-prompt use cases seen in production. It takes precedence
over defaultMaxPrefixBlocks: maxBlocks = defaultMaxPrefixTokens / blockSizeTokens.

prefill profile name to ensure that the index is updated for the prefill endpoint and not
only for the primary endpoint that will initially handle the request.
This is hardcoded for now until we land on a canonical approach for plugins to identify
prefill and decode endpoints (See https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api-inference-extension/issues/2080)

operator_config.name: pruneEngineKeyScript
operator_config.value:
redis.NewScript(`
	for i = 2, #KEYS do
		if redis.call('HLEN', KEYS[i]) > 0 then
			return 0
		end
	end
	redis.call('DEL', KEYS[1])
	return 1
`)
operator_config.doc:
pruneEngineKeyScript atomically deletes an engine key mapping only if all
associated request key hashes are empty. This prevents a TOCTOU race where a
concurrent Add could insert into a request key between checking and deleting.
KEYS[1] = engine key ("engine:<hash>"), KEYS[2..N] = request key hashes.

	end
	return 0
`)

operator_config.name: noDataParallelRank
operator_config.doc:
noDataParallelRank is the sentinel data-parallel rank used in a dedup scope.

On current main the index identity (kvblock.PodEntry) is pod-level and does
NOT distinguish data-parallel ranks, so every scope uses this sentinel and
reference counts aggregate across ranks — which is exactly what the pod-level
index requires (a block is still resident on the pod until every rank has
removed it). The value matches PR #370's NoDataParallelRank (-1) convention.

TODO(#370): once DataParallelRank is propagated onto EventBatch and into
PodEntry, source the rank from the event in pool.go so the dedup scope
becomes DP-aware in lockstep with the (then DP-aware) index identity. No
change to this file is required — only the scope construction at the call
sites.

operator_config.name: noGroupIdx
operator_config.doc:
noGroupIdx is the sentinel groupIdx used in a dedup scope when an event
carries no KV-cache group. It mirrors the "no group" PodEntry state
(HasGroup=false), so grouped and ungrouped copies of the same block hash are
reference-counted independently — matching how the index treats them as
distinct entries. Real event group indices are non-negative (the engine
adapters reject a negative group_idx), so this sentinel cannot collide with a
genuine group.
